items.title: Two Breaches, One Lesson: Why Your Security Program Can’t Rely on Trust
items.summary: A record $6.3 billion crypto theft and a university-wide shutdown hit within two weeks of each other. Different victims, same weakness: trust that was granted once and never re-examined. Here’s what both incidents show, and four controls to check this month.

items.title: The 450% Problem: How AI Annihilated Your Patch Window
items.summary: AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery and shrinking the window between patch and exploit. Here’s how to prepare your defenses before disclosure.

items.title: BYOD Ransomware: An Identity-First Extortion Campaign Moving Into Hospitals and Universities
items.summary: In about five weeks, a new ransomware group called BYOD went from small businesses to a trauma center and two major U.S. universities. Here’s what we know and what to hunt for now.

items.title: What the Blue Wave Means for AI Regulation
items.summary: Congress is poised to set new AI rules. Tom Kellermann outlines five areas to watch, from AI agent governance to workforce preparation, and what defenders can do now.

items.title: Beyond Zero Day: Minus One and the New Era of Predictive Cyber Defense
PaperWall Unmasked: A Disguised News Network Now Reaching AI Search Results
items.summary: New TrendAI™ Research report finds PaperWall, a network of fake local news sites, has expanded to nearly 200 newly identified domains and is now surfacing in AI-assisted search results.

items.title: From a Docker Ping to an AI Command Plane: Inside the Hermes Attack Workbench and Carbonato Model Gateway — Part 2: Operations
items.summary: In this second part of our research, we provide our analysis of the Hermes session records, revealing how the threat operation coordinated AI agents, updated attack methods, and targeted multiple services beyond Docker.

items.title: When AI Agents Trust the Dead: More Than 900 MCP Servers Pointing to Hijackable GitHub Repositories
items.summary: We examined more than 90,000 GitHub URLs across four major MCP directories and found links that point to deleted accounts; the usernames of these can be claimed by anyone, including attackers. AI agents serving as installers complicate the matter further, raising questions about trust and security.

items.title: The 90/10 Principle: Why AI Transformation Starts with Process, Not Technology
items.summary: Good processes plus AI equals accelerated excellence. Bad processes plus AI equals accelerated chaos.

items.title: From a Docker Ping to an AI Command Plane: Inside the Hermes Attack Workbench and Carbonato Model Gateway — Part 1: Discovery
items.summary: Attack attempts against our Docker honeypot led us to uncover AI-assisted attack infrastructure combining AI agents and other offensive tools. We examine its components, security implications, and how organizations can mitigate the risks.

items.title: The Lone Wolf AI Attacker Won't Stay Alone for Long
items.summary: AI helped one attacker breach more than 100 companies for about $50 each. The bigger risk is who inherits that access next.

items.title: An AI Wrote a Remote Root Exploit for Linux: What CVE-2026-98432 Means for Defenders
items.summary: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical Linux kernel TCP flaw that Anthropic says its unreleased AI model turned into a working remote root exploit.
